title: Virtual table: compact mode and resize gesture rework
creator: Ava Moreno
description: Scope: Redesign the compact (high-density) mode of the virtualized table and overhaul the column-resize gesture model to be predictable, accessible, and performant across host/dedicated/private deployments. This ticket covers: interaction specs, visual tokens, keyboard & screen-reader semantics, motion timing for virtualization handoff, and a small prototype to validate ergonomics. Problem: Current compact mode compresses spacing but causes unstable column reflow when users resize columns while scrolling; keyboard resize is inconsistent and screen reader announcements are ambiguous. Goals: 1) make a deterministic resize model that avoids layout thrashing during continuous scrolling; 2) provide an explicit compact density token set; 3) unify mouse, touch, and keyboard resize interactions; 4) document accessibility behaviour and telemetry hooks for engineering.
decisions: Introduce a dedicated density token set: density.compact.{rowHeight,cellPadding,fontScale} rather than ad-hoc CSS overrides
Adopt a two-stage resize interaction: live-preview for small drags (<8px) and displacement-on-release for larger drags to avoid continuous reflow during virtualization
Keyboard resize will use modifier+arrow keys (Ctrl+Alt+Arrow) with visible aria-live announcements and a short debounce before committing size to avoid frequent re-render
Sticky column support will be limited to soft-sticky (visual overlay) in compact mode for performance reasons; full DOM sticky columns deferred to ENG-82910
tradeoffs: Two-stage resize reduces immediate WYSIWYG feel but dramatically lowers layout churn under heavy virtualization
Soft-sticky columns are less robust for complex pinned headers but avoid forcing sticky layout inside the virtualized window (improves throughput)
Debounced keyboard commits introduce a small delay for power users but prevent input spamming and reduce snapshots for telemetry
tasks: Complete low-fidelity gesture sketches and present at weekly design critique (done 2025-02-24)
Build interactive Figma prototype for compact mode and resize model (in progress)
Define density token table and update design token spec (rowHeight, padding, fontScale)
Write accessibility spec: aria roles, live-region messages, focus management, and keyboard shortcuts
Coordinate with ENG: align on virtualization boundary (ENG-81234) and soft-sticky feasibility (ENG-82910)
Run moderated usability sessions (4 participants) focusing on resizing in dense tables
Create a lightweight visual QA checklist and add to console-2025.03 release criteria
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype demonstrates both small-drag live-preview and displacement-on-release behaviours
Design token set for compact mode merged into tokens spec and reviewed by Design System owners
Accessibility doc contains keyboard shortcut, aria-live sample phrases, and SR testing checklist
Engineering signals: ENG-81234 implements a version of two-stage resize with <10ms average frame drop on 2s continuous drag in dev perf harness
Telemetry hooks defined for: resize-start, resize-commit, density-toggle, and keyboard-resize events
Design review approval by PM (Ravi Patel) and Engineering lead (Marcus Yi)
notes: Usability: 3 of 4 participants preferred the displacement-on-release when scrolling; one participant expected immediate column width change (power-user) — consider optional 'live-resize' toggle behind feature flag
Performance: initial dev harness shows jitter when live-updating width during high-velocity scroll; mitigation by deferring commit until scroll stabilizes suggested
Accessibility: screen reader text should announce 'Column width preview: 120px' during live-preview and 'Column width set to 120px' on commit
Follow-ups: add a telemetry event for feature-flag usage; PM to decide on exposing live-resize toggle in settings (PM-274)
QA: include tests for keyboard-resize repeat and focus trapping inside column header popover
